Product Design · B2B SaaS · Travel Tech

Redesigning Xeni's
Command Centre

From a fragmented, single-tenant legacy platform to a scalable enterprise command centre — ready for multi-agency operations and role-based access control.

00Overview

The platform that outgrew itself

Xeni is a travel SaaS platform built to help agencies sell travel products — hotels, flights, activities, and more — via code or no-code integrations. As the platform matured and enterprise clients began evaluating it, a fundamental gap became clear: the product was architecturally and experientially not scaling for multi-tenant, enterprise-grade use.

Over years of organic feature additions, the system had accumulated deep structural debt — duplicated modules, inconsistent patterns, hidden functionality, and no role management. The result: lost deals in the high-value B2B segment and daily friction for power users.

The brief: Redesign the entire Command Centre experience — from information architecture and navigation to the dashboard, tables, onboarding, and role management — to unlock enterprise adoption and reduce operational friction for existing customers.

01Design Process

Double Diamond, rigorously applied

This project followed the Double Diamond framework across four phases. Each phase had a defined objective, method set, and output before proceeding to the next.

Phase 01

Discover

Primary research, design audit, competitive analysis, Clarity heatmaps

Phase 02

Define

Card sorting, personas, pain point mapping, use case framing

Phase 03

Develop

IA restructure, feature prioritisation, wireframes, AI-assisted prototyping

Phase 04

Deliver

High-fidelity designs, validated flows, handoff documentation

02Discovery

Listening before designing

The Discover phase was about building an honest picture of the current state — not just what the product does, but how real users experience it and where it consistently fails them.

Primary research — stakeholder sessions

Discussion and feedback sessions were run across five organisational functions: Product, Business, Customer Success, Design, and Engineering.

Brainstorming & mind mapping

Parallel brainstorming sessions mapped the full problem space — covering navigation structure, feature ownership, and open questions around Wallet, multi-tenancy, and commission reporting.

Design audit — existing information architecture

The existing product was mapped end-to-end to document the legacy IA, identify overlapping modules, and surface hidden or underused features.

Pain points identified

Research synthesis surfaced eight core pain areas, each categorised by area and severity.

Dashboard
No drill-down capability. Lacks operational and financial clarity. Commission data lived in a separate, disconnected view.
Critical
Data Tables
No column freezing. Too many visible columns (24+). Hard to scan, causing horizontal scroll fatigue.
Critical
Clients & Agents
No clear hierarchy. Performance visibility missing. Custom markup data buried and hard to surface.
High
Searches Module
Purely an analytics log — no ability to act on a search result, contact a client, or trigger follow-up actions.
High
Payments & Subscriptions
No subscription history, no downloadable invoices. Payout onboarding captured via external Google Form.
High
Information Architecture
Poor grouping, unclear mental model, too many top-level nav items, duplicated modules.
Critical
Role Management
No custom role or permission model — a hard blocker for enterprise adoption.
Enterprise Blocker
Multi-tenancy
Single-tenant only. No ability for an organisation to manage multiple agency accounts under one roof.
Enterprise Blocker
03Define

Turning noise into signal

The Define phase transformed raw feedback into structured design direction — shaping who we were designing for, what mattered most, and what questions needed answering before development.

Card sorting sessions

Raw feedback was card sorted using proximity grouping to identify natural clusters across bookings data, dashboard widgets, and module-level groupings.

User personas

AO
Agency Owner / CTO
52 · Travel Agency Leadership
Goal

Add and manage users with custom roles and permissions across one or more agencies under a single organisation.

Frustration

No role management means every user has the same access — a security and operational risk for enterprise accounts.

PM
Product Manager / CX Support
38 · Onboarding & Technical Ops
Goal

Provide technical assistance during customer onboarding and manage subscriptions effectively.

Frustration

Tables are hard to use due to excessive columns; subscription history is absent, making billing support nearly impossible.

SM
Sales & CX Support Manager
47 · Revenue & Customer Operations
Goal

Handle cancellation requests efficiently and have real visibility into booking status and client activity.

Frustration

Booking management forms are too long; dashboard gives no operational view of what's happening right now.

Before development began, the team aligned on strategic questions: Do we need Wallet at all? Can Commission be part of the Dashboard? Should Deals and Proposals be unified? Should Searches remain a separate module? These were resolved through feature prioritisation and IA restructuring.

04Develop

Restructuring from the ground up

The Develop phase translated research and definition into concrete design solutions — starting with the architecture before touching pixels.

Feature prioritisation & categorisation

All identified features were plotted and prioritised by impact and feasibility, then categorised into the new module groupings.

Information architecture restructure

The restructure applied a single principle: group by user mental model, not by technical module boundaries.

Legacy ItemRestructured Outcome
Monthly Commission (standalone)→Integrated into Dashboard as widget
Deals + Proposals (separate modules)→Unified under single conceptual model
Wallet (primary nav)→Marked optional / removable per agency
Xeni Academy (primary nav)→Moved under User Profile
Separate Command Centre page→Removed — merged logically into platform
Searches (read-only log)→Connected to actionable flows (email, campaign)
No role management→New Roles & Permissions module under Settings
Single-tenant org model→Multi-tenant: Org Owner → Multiple Agencies

Finalised information architecture

A clean two-tier structure: a global Org Console for organisation-level management, and an Agency Command Centre for agency-level operations.

Navigation redesign

The new model uses icon-based navigation with grouped modules and a flattened top-level structure — down from 13+ items to 7 grouped modules.

Dashboard: from summary to command centre

Before
  • Static KPI cards only
  • No drill-down capability
  • Commission shown separately
  • No booking category breakdown
  • No upcoming trips visibility
  • No financial + operational split
After
  • Clickable KPI cards with drill-down
  • Category-based stats (Hotels, Flights)
  • Monthly commission graph integrated
  • Upcoming trip overview widget
  • Revenue + booking trend charts
  • Quick Report — monthly download option

Wireframing with AI augmentation

Initial concept sketches mapped organisational structure and flow logic on the whiteboard, then rapidly prototyped using Lovable for idea validation before moving into high-fidelity Figma wireframes.

View Lovable Prototype

Prototyping approach: Whiteboard sketching → Lovable prototype for concept validation → Figma wireframes → high-fidelity UI. Design decisions were validated at the lowest possible fidelity before investment in polished screens.

05Final Design

The redesigned platform, screen by screen

The following screens represent the final high-fidelity Figma designs delivered — covering both the Org Console (multi-tenant management layer) and the Agency Command Centre (day-to-day operations layer).

Org Console — multi-tenant layer

The Org Console is a new top-tier layer introduced to support multi-tenancy. Organisation owners can view overall performance across all agencies and manage accounts from a single view.

Org · Dashboard
Overall agencies performance — commission by product, confirmed vs. cancelled bookings, total booking volume across all accounts.
Org · Accounts
All agency accounts under one organisation — domain, plan type (OTA / API), payment method, and creation date visible at a glance.

Agency Command Centre — operations layer

The redesigned core interface for day-to-day operations, reflecting the pain point resolution work throughout the process.

Agency · Dashboard
Booking trend chart, upcoming trips calendar with drill-down by product type, and recent bookings table.
Agency · Bookings
Bookings table with product-type tabs (Hotels, Flights, Cars, Activities, Resorts), frozen primary column, compact/detail view toggle.
Agency · Monthly Commissions
Commission by product breakdown with donut chart, confirmed/cancelled bookings overview, total booking volume, and downloadable report.

Clients management

Clients
Clients list with overview KPIs (Total, Active, Payment Approval pending, Seats usage), inline status indicators, bulk upload, and export CSV.

Settings — Profile & Website customisation

Settings · Profile
Profile settings — personal information, home location, and email address change.
Settings · Website
Website Settings with live preview — brand logo, theme, banners, top destinations, address, social links all on one page.
